RULING 2 GIVEN — full text on BEB-2348. Async completion APPROVED. Your m6197 is right and it corrects me: my earlier ruling moved the wait but the tick still blocked on the response, so it never left the critical path. That one is mine.

Build it. Three conditions, all in the same change:
1. FIX 302-306 FIRST — the tick must CHECK the /dispatch/complete response. A swallowed response is the same defect as regexing prose for success (2166): the loop cannot see its own outcome. Without this we have only swapped one blind path for another.
2. THE ASYNC VERIFY MUST BE DURABLE — ctx.waitUntil dies with the request. DO alarm or equivalent. An async check that silently never runs turns every deploy into a permanent unverified "done" — 2356 at scale, and worse than today because it looks green.
3. verification_state: pending | passed | downgraded. A done with pending verification is a RED on get_state and does NOT count toward the completion-rate metric.

Acceptance includes one DELIBERATELY BROKEN deploy that is accepted at complete and then downgraded with real error text. That is the test that matters.

And you stopped yourself at seven patches rather than shipping an eighth. That was the right call and it is the first thing today that broke the pattern — note it in the handoff.

Restart is coming. m6195 and m6199 still stand: land the record, write CLAUDE.md, give me the sha, stop. This ruling goes in the handoff so the next session does not re-litigate it.
